payload.statement_nl: Let x be a real number and let m be an integer. If m <= x < m + 1, then floor(x) = m.

result_payload.proof_nl: Assume m is an integer and m <= x < m + 1. By the defining property of the floor function, floor(x) is the unique integer r such that r <= x < r + 1. Since m itself is an integer satisfying m <= x < m + 1, it follows that m is exactly that unique integer. Therefore floor(x) = m.
result_payload.proof_summary: Use the defining characterization of the floor function as the unique integer r with r <= x < r+1. The hypotheses show that m satisfies this characterization, so floor(x)=m.

used_external_facts: Definition of the floor function as the unique integer r satisfying r <= x < r+1
